articleTitle: Kidney Disease Classification and Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Review of Current AI Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Accurate and early diagnosis of kidney disease (KD) is crucial for effective treatment and improved patient outcomes. computer aided and AI techniques offers a promising solution in this domain, analyzing medical images to identify disease patterns. This research paper explores the potential of ML, particularly deep learning (DL) and transfer learning, for classifying kidney conditions from CT scans. We review existing research to identify the most effective ai algorithms for this task, evaluate performance metrics used to assess accuracy, and explore challenges like data availability and interpretability. By discussing future directions, including integration of additional data sources, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive analysis of AI techniques-based KD classification, paving the way for more accurate and efficient diagnostic tools.

articleTitle: FusionAraSA: Fusion-based Model for Accurate Arabic Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: The Arabic language is one of the most common spoken languages. Due to the complex structure and extensive range of potential meanings of Arabic texts, it is a challenging task to perform sentiment analysis using Natural Language Processing (NLP) approaches. Traditional methods of sentiment analysis often fail to perform Arabic sentiment analysis tasks. In this study, a fusion majority voting technique was employed to enhance the performance of Arabic sentiment analysis. The proposed method integrates four models (i.e. AraBERv1, MARBERT, Modified MARBERT, and AraBERv2 ) to analyze Arabic sentiments. Then, the outputs of these four models were forwarded to a fusion stage the perform majority voting and show the corresponding identified class. This technique is called FusionAraSA which relies on integrating four models and fusion to expand the application of pre-trained models. The FusionAraSA approach shows promising performance reaching more than 95% in terms of both accuracy and F1 Score utilizing two publicly available Arabic datasets. The results obtained using FusionAraSA illustrate the exceptional performance and the feasibility of this model in Arabic sentiment analysis. Additionally, the findings highlight the remarkable potential of the fusion model and underscore the necessity for further research to unravel the intricacies of Arabic dialects. Moreover, the FusionAraSA model represents a major step towards building more complex, culturally sensitive, and technologically advanced Arabic language analysis architecture.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Sentiment Analysis of Twitter Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Sentiment Analysis plays a pivotal role in modern business operations, including analyzing and monitoring textual data. This paper presents a comparative analysis of various machine learning models for sentiment analysis of Twitter data. The models explored include Decision Tree, KNN classifier, Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naïve Bayes, and Random Forest Classifier. Emphasizing the significance of preprocessing and vectorization techniques for feature extraction, the study delves into hyperparameter tuning to optimize each model’s performance. Evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and ROC analysis highlight the Random Forest Classifier demonstrating the highest accuracy. These findings underscore the efficacy of machine learning methodologies in sentiment analysis tasks and offer valuable insights for enhancing model performance in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluation of Pre-trained Deep Learning Models for Efficient Arabic Sign Language Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Yemeni Sign Language (YSL) is a vital communication means for the deaf-muted Yemen community. The deaf-mute community in Yemen faces communication obstacles due to limited access to several environments such as education, work, and social activities. In addition, there are no datasets available for Yemeni sign language. This study is designed to overcome some of the current limitations of Yemeni Sign Language by extending a new dataset for the Yemeni Sign Language dataset and investigating the efficiency of recent transfer learning approaches for YSL recognition. This study compared the effectiveness of transfer learning techniques in the context of YSL recognition. Deep learning models adopted are AlexNet, ResNet152V2, Swin Transformer, InceptionV3, and Xception. These models were selected due to their performance reported by previous research within a diverse computer vision task. The new dataset was constructed with 24,245 sign images collected manually with specific criteria to obtain 32 different sign labels. A preprocessing for sign images was applied to improve the recognition process of the YSL sign. CNN models are customized using transfer learning and fine-tuning strategies for experimental purposes. Experiment results showed a remarkable accuracy rate for Swin Transformer, AlexNet, InceptionV3, ResNet152V2, and Xception models as 99.0%, 99.0%, 98,0%, 98.0%, and 99.0%, respectively. The study result showed that The Xception model obtained the highest training accuracy rate, and the AlexNet and Swin transformer models obtained the highest testing accuracy rate. In conclusion, the outcomes contribute to developing a robust and accessible YSL recognition system to prompt effective communication and inclusivity for the deaf-muted community in Yemen.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of Intelligent Techniques for Obstetric Complication Prediction in the Last 20 Years
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of intelligent techniques in predicting obstetric complications over the past 20 years. These complications significantly impact maternal and neonatal health, necessitating early prediction and management. The study highlights the growing use of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) in this field. By reviewing literature from 2004 to 2023, it identifies a gap in research focused on using intelligent techniques for predicting obstetric complications. Keyword co-occurrence analysis reveals significant research clusters in areas like diabetes mellitus, biomarkers, and treatment management. The study emphasizes the need for practical ML-based applications to aid clinical decision-making and suggests that trend data should inform curriculum development and clinical practice guidelines in obstetrics.

articleTitle: Data Integration in Big Data Environment: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Big Data Analytics (BDA) has been one of the top strategic technology directions in the last decade and one of the most significant trends that is transforming organizational processes and operations throughout the world. With the proven potential of Big Data, corporate investments have been increasing significantly. However, implementing BDA is a complex process that involves many challenges. Big Data Integration (BDI), which involves the consolidation of data from various sources, is among the most significant and frequent challenges encountered in any Big Data Analytics project. It is also regarded as a critical factor in determining the success of BDA initiatives. In this paper, the authors conducted a review of existing Big Data Integration (BDI) literature with three primary objectives: first, to define BDI and distinguish it from traditional data integration; second, to outline various influential factors mentioned in prior studies and categorize them according to their characteristics; and finally, to identify and highlight the gaps within the current body of literature on this critical topic. The review found that there is still a dearth of study in this area, with just a small amount of literature devoted to examining this crucial problem and few empirical investigations that rely on accepted theories. Further research is needed to overcome these shortcomings.

articleTitle: The Influence of E-Customer Service, Mobile Application Design, Brand Image, and Customer Satisfaction on Interest in Mobile Banking Adoption
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Mobile banking competition is an important issue for companies in acquiring customers. The success of technology implementation in organizations often depends on the extent to which users can accept and utilize it effectively. Therefore, assessing the level of interest in adoption of BSI Mobile becomes very important. When an app is introduced, users' attitudes towards the app, whether positive or negative, are based on how they perceive the app. This study aims to analyze the direct and indirect effects of e-customer service, brand image, mobile application design, and customer satisfaction on interest in mobile banking adoption. This study analyzed 96 respondents of bsi mobile service user customers using quantitative methods and SEM PLS analysis techniques using the SmartPLS application. The results of this study indicate e-customer service, mobile application design, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on user satisfaction. User satisfaction significantly mediates the influence of e-customer service, mobile application design, and brand image. Then, user satisfaction has a positive and significant effect on increasing customer interest in using BSI Mobile.

articleTitle: Real-Time Diabetes Detection Using Machine Learning and Apache Spark
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: The convergence of contemporary and cutting-edge technologies, including big data analytics and machine learning, is reshaping the scale and efficiency of healthcare systems. This work presents distinct approaches and contributions, addressing specific challenges in healthcare and disease and diabetes analytics. The real-time healthcare for disease diabetes and the integration of big data analytics, machine learning, and real-time processing have paved the way for innovative solutions to address disease diabetes prediction and monitoring. It’s explored innovative solutions to overcome challenges in healthcare analytics, offering real-time predictions and continuous monitoring for improved patient care. The real-time Healthcare-Diabetes dataset was analyzed using various machine learning models, and processing in real-time has led to innovative solutions to address diabetes prediction and monitoring. The Gradient Boosted Tree Classifier emerged as the most accurate model with an accuracy of 90.14%, followed by the Decision Tree Classifier at 84.62%, the Random Forest Classifier at 82.84%, the Linear Support Vector Classifier at 78.70%, and Logistic Regression at 64.69%. These results demonstrate the system’s robustness and efficiency in real-time data collection, processing, and prediction. Leveraging Apache Spark and open-source big data technologies, specify data challenges and advocate for scalable, efficient, and cost-effective healthcare analytics. It contributes to the ongoing transformation of healthcare systems, demonstrating the effectiveness of advanced technologies in enhancing disease prediction, monitoring, and overall healthcare services.

articleTitle: Beauty Formula DermoScan: user-centric skincare products’ ingredient analysis platform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: daily skincare routines play a pivotal role in determining the long-term health and appearance of one's skin. The presence of synthetic chemicals in numerous skincare products can lead to various adverse effects for consumers, which may result in skin allergies. Consequently, a deep understanding of skincare products and their ingredients becomes essential. This knowledge empowers individuals to craft personalized skincare regimens that effectively target their unique concerns and complement the professional care they receive. This research addresses the limited accessibility of information about the intricate chemical compositions of skincare products for consumers and stakeholders. In response, this study integrates Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology, machine learning algorithms; TF-IDF text matching technique and KNN text categorization algorithm, and visualization techniques. The overarching goal is to establish a user-centric website, "Beauty Formula DermoScan," providing a seamless solution for users to comprehend skincare ingredients. Through a simple photo upload, users receive detailed and easily understandable insights into the product's composition. This comprehensive approach seeks to revolutionize the skincare industry by fostering transparency, efficiency, and a knowledge-driven ecosystem. Beauty Formula DermoScan can redefine how both consumers and the industry perceive and engage with skincare ingredients, offering a transformative platform for informed decision-making.

articleTitle: Influence of Model UTAUT 2 and Confidence on User Interest in OVO Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: E-wallet is a temporary wallet that has funds in an online application, which allows users to perform cashless transactions with their digital accounts in web applications. This research focuses on the UTAUT 2 model and trust variables to find and analyze the factors that influence user interest in the OVO application. A total of 96 OVO app users were administered an online questionnaire. The data was analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Square (PLS-SEM) with Smart-PLS.3 software. The results showed that of the 12 hypotheses tested, 7 were accepted and 5 were rejected. The accepted hypotheses include the variables Continuance Usage Intention affects Continuance Usage Behavior, Effort Expectancy affects Performance Expectancy, Facilitating Conditions affects Continuance Usage Behavior, Hedonic Motivation affects Continuance Usage Intention, Performance Expectancy affects Continuance Usage Intention, and Trust affects Continuance Usage Intention and Performance Expectancy. While the variables Effort Expectancy, Facilitating Conditions, Hedonic Motivation, Price Value do not have a significant effect on Continuance Usage Intention and Continuance Usage Behavior. According to this study, the variables of Habit, Performance Expectancy and Trust are very important for user satisfaction and continuance usage behavior. Improving these factors in the future can help retain and attract more users to e-wallet applications.

articleTitle: Agile Ontology: A Dynamic Framework for E-Business Evolution
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: In this work, a progressed version of Extreme Programming (XP) for e-business is provided. In an effort to efficiently address the precise troubles of this dynamic industry, the strategy promotes iterative procedures and more functions. By including new elements that guide growth, independence, and fine manipulation, Enhanced XP for E-business (EXPe) builds upon the fundamental XP concepts of continuous feedback and collaboration. The e-business enterprise faces challenges such as rapidly evolving marketplace needs and the want for scalable, adaptive solutions. EXPe targets to cope with these by using selling iterative development and incorporating more suitable functionalities to help non-stop adaptation and scalability. The layout prioritizes user standards, adds more scalability mechanisms, and employs iterative improvement techniques to help development teams adapt quickly and efficaciously to changing E-enterprise desires. This study indicates that EXPe is a great choice for quickly and efficaciously growing E-business solutions due to its many benefits and capabilities. This technique aims to provide a strong foundation for engaging in non-intrusive studies on agile methods. Enhanced XP for E-Business (EXPe) uniquely integrates ontology-unique requirements and semantic research into the agile framework, extensively enhancing the adaptability and scalability of e-commercial enterprise solutions. Furthermore, listed for this purpose are applicable files and XP artifacts, including user stories.

articleTitle: AI-Empowered Peatland Management for Climate-Resilient and Sustainable Future: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Peatlands are crucial for preserving biodiversity, controlling temperatures and storing carbon on a scale. The vital ecological systems face threats from the degradation of land and deforestation, which leads to impacts of climate change, while Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays a vital role in effectively addressing the challenges. By exploring how AI supports monitoring peatlands and climate change, we propose a novel framework that integrates AI and peatland management in order to bolster climate resilience and sustainability efforts based on evidence. Therefore, policymakers can improve the peatland restoration, monitoring and conservation programs by leveraging AI for data analysis, predictive modelling and decision-making processes. AI enables real-time tracking of peatland conditions, detecting activities and wildfires, and optimizing land management strategies. Through the presentation of case studies and best practices, this study underscores how incorporating AI-driven policies for peatland management can strengthen ecosystem sustainability and climate resilience.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection in Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs): A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) have become a key security problem due to the increasing number of connected automobiles and the sensitive nature of the data transferred in Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs). By keeping an eye on network traffic, spotting questionable activity, and putting countermeasures in place to lessen risks, IDSs protect the integrity and security of VANETs. For VANETs, this study explores the state-of-the-art in machine learning-based IDSs, with a particular emphasis on work released in 2020–2022. We provide a thorough analysis of developments in widely used machine learning methods used for VANET intrusion detection throughout this time. This investigation explores certain machine learning methods that have been recently applied to VANET IDSs. The survey ends with a summary of the current issues and an exploration of potential directions for further investigation.

articleTitle: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence Bias In Answering Religious Questions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Question Answering (QA) is a specialized field in the field of NLP and most studies in this field focus on the English language, while other languages, such as Arabic, are still in their early stages. Recently, research has turned to developing answering systems for Questions for Arabic-Islamic texts, which may impose challenges due to the nature of the Arabic language and due to the lack and scarcity of reference data sets. Research has also tended to develop systems to answer open-ended questions that aim to extract the answer to the user’s question from a specific text or from a specific context in this study. We evaluated artificial intelligence to answer religious questions to facilitate access to religious information. We created a fatwa dataset consisting of questions and answers from approved websites. We used the transformer-based Arabic language generation model AraGPT2, and we reconfigured the answer generation task, as our approach provides answers to questions by generating... The answer is among the answers on which the model was trained, and there is no context available to extract the answer from. This is what is known as the system for answering closed-field questions. Then we evaluated the resulting model using the evaluation methods, which are BERTScore, Levenshtein distance, and BLEU. The proposed model achieved the best evaluation score of 0.73 on the BERTScore scale, which indicates Good performance. In addition, the performance results were analyzed to determine the strengths and weaknesses of the model. The researchers suggest improving the model's performance by expanding the data set, modifying the model structure, and applying human evaluation of the model.

articleTitle: An Ocean Wave Power Plant Buoy System as Learning Media
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: This study aims to develop a prototype of an ocean wave power plant buoy system as an educational tool to introduce the concept of renewable energy to students. The authors use a v-model, which includes design stages, implementation, calibration test, and validation. The calibration focuses on observing the influence of wave amplitude on electrical current output, while the validation tests by experts use instrument item validity tests. Results from the calibration test indicated that larger wave amplitudes produced higher electrical currents, with significant precision and standard deviation calculations confirming the reliability of the measurements. The validation test results categorised the learning media as very good based on presentation, visual, and design aspects, with an overall score indicating high suitability for educational use. Educating future generations about renewable energy sources like ocean waves is crucial with the increasing global demand for sustainable energy solutions. Existing educational tools often lack hands-on experience, limiting students' understanding of complex concepts. This prototype aims to fill that gap by providing a tangible learning experience demonstrating ocean wave energy conversion into electricity. By integrating STEM principles into education through practical applications, because it involves a combination of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics, students can better appreciate renewable energy technologies and their potential impact on global energy sustainability.

articleTitle: Predicting Child Development Status: Can Machine Learning Help?
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) has recently been used to solve different problems including detection of child development status, meeting children’s individual learning needs, detecting and intervening developmental problems early, improving rehabilitation processes, and so on. Hence, in this study, we build and use ML models to predict the development status of children based on a recently shared dataset that includes various attributes. To improve the performance of our models, we applied simple and efficient imputing, feature extension, and enlarging techniques on the dataset. The results show that four of ten ML algorithms reach the perfect performance (i.e., an f1-score of 1.0) and this indicates that ML is capable of solving this problem in an automatic and highly accurate way. We therefore believe that the findings of this study can uncover the applicability of ML to solve problems within the related field.

articleTitle: Direction of Machine Learning Research in Obstetric Care in the Last 10 Years
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: This study aims to use bibliometric analysis to examine how machine learning research trends in obstetric care have evolved over time. First, 829 publications from 2014 to 2023 were collected from the Web of Science database. The fundamental issues and characteristics of machine learning in obstetric care research were analyzed, such as annual publication contribution and focus, using theme analysis, concurrency analysis, and topic trend analysis. Second, productive objects, such as journals, authors, institutions, countries, regions, and Collaborative relationship mapping, are used to present who is leading the considerable attention in machine learning research in obstetric care. Third, the citation structure of authors and journals was investigated, and references were cited. This Bibliometric analysis revealed an increasing annual publication trend, a shift in focus to machine learning in obstetric care, the dominance of authors from China, and an increasing number of international collaborations, indicating machine learning in obstetric care as a vibrant and growing field and need for further scientific enrichment. Therefore, a comprehensive study on machine learning in obstetric care reviews the characteristics and trajectory of current research and helps scholars find suitable research entry points and conduct in-depth research.

articleTitle: Buildings Energy Efficiency Assessment: Case Study of Aden Apartment House
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Because the gap between energy supply and rising demand expands, reducing energy consumption and improving efficiency are critical to addressing the energy crisis in Yemen. This study develops an energy audit method to lower costs and environmental impact for apartments in Aden, Yemen. An in-depth audit of a two-room flat examines potential savings through optimal equipment usage and preventative measures. Different retrofit, appliance, glass, and shading scenarios were modeled using design builder software to balance daylight, thermal comfort, and minimal energy use. Findings show heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) and lighting upgrades can provide adaptive thermal comfort while increasing efficiency. Proposed renovation measures investigate conservation options in hot and humid climates. The findings show that the house's dominant source of thermal heat gain came from the AC unit. The optimization method in design demonstrates how building envelopes can ensure performance and comfort with energy reduction. Applying this method to the Yemeni apartments cuts annual energy costs from $1906 to $1637, resulting in a 14.11 % savings of 269 $ through more efficient operations.

articleTitle: Kinect Therapeutic Game STEAM-Based Learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Students
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) experience difficulties in their learning process because they have impairments in cognitive development, adaptive behaviour, focus/attention, and psychomotor problems. Using technology-based learning media can be an effective solution in helping ASD students overcome their learning challenges. This research aims to develop the "Kinect Therapeutic Games" learning media by integrating STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Mathematics). The ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation) approach was the development model used in developing the media. Six ASD students at Special School Mitra Amanda in Surakarta, Indonesia, were the subjects of this research. The result shows that achieving by using the learning media also requires a good balance of psychomotor, attention, and cognitive abilities. For Science, Technology, and Engineering, as many as 4 out of 6 students or more than half of the students in one class, have good results. Only 2 out of 6 students, or 33,33%, have good numeracy skills when using the learning media. Half or 50% of students in a class could achieve aspects of art related to imagination and creativity. It can be concluded that learning media can support STEAM aspects, but not all students can achieve them. Only 2 out of 6 students could accomplish all of the STEAM aspects.

articleTitle: Cloud Computing Adoption Among Small and Medium Entrprises (SMEs) in Kuwait: a Preliminary Qualitative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Cloud Computing (CC) is a contemporary model that offers organizations access to advanced computing services via the Internet, with payment based on usage and on-demand availability. Numerous research studies have established that CC enables Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) to leverage modern information technology services at minimal costs, thereby positively impacting their business performance. SMEs play a crucial role in contributing to the economic growth of countries. However, there is a lack of published studies on the status of Cloud Computing Adoption (CCA) among SMEs in Kuwait. A preliminary study was undertaken to examine the state of CCA among Kuwaiti SMEs and the determining factors in the process of CCA in Kuwait. The study revealed a low level of CCA among Kuwaiti SMEs, as well as a low level of Intention to Adopt Cloud Computing (IACC) among those SMEs not currently utilizing any CC services. The determining factors in the CCA process among Kuwaiti SMEs were identified as perceived benefits, security concerns, competitive pressure, trading partner pressure, top management support, social influence, innovativeness, and risk-taking. Consequently, the preliminary study recommended that further in-depth studies be conducted to gain a better understanding of the issues affecting the IACC among SMEs in Kuwait.

articleTitle: Imaging Modalities in Brain Cancer Detection and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Brain cancer is a highly heterogeneous and complex illness, making diagnosis and treatment extremely difficult. The purpose of this study is to clarify how different data types—such as imaging, genomic, proteomic, and clinical data—affect brain tumor characterizations and therapeutic decision-making. This research explores the application of customized medicine, the molecular categorization of brain tumors, and the monitoring of disease progression. Additionally, a comparative examination of various imaging modalities, including fMRI, MRI, CT, PET, and SPECT, is conducted. As a result, this study highlights the importance of many data kinds in tracking disease development, identifying brain tumor subtypes, and devising tailored treatments. These data types include imaging, genomic, proteomic, and clinical data. It also emphasizes the difficulties and possibilities associated with combining multimodal data, with the goal of stimulating more research on the identification and management of brain cancer. Ultimately, the analysis highlights the current obstacles and potential paths for combining and evaluating multimodal data to improve the prognosis for brain cancer.

articleTitle: Predicting System Availability: A Comparative Study of Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and Regression Analysis Models in a Food Factory
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average ARIMA and regression analysis models in predicting system availability within a food factory context. The primary research question explores which model provides more accurate and reliable predictions for system availability, thereby aiding in maintenance planning and operational efficiency. The methodology involves collecting and analyzing three years of daily operational data, including system uptime, idle time, downtime, and overall availability. Both ARIMA and regression models are developed and compared based on evaluation metrics such as mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). The findings indicate that the regression model achieve better than ARIMA. The study concludes that while both models have significant potential for improving maintenance planning, their effectiveness depends on the specific data characteristics and operational requirements of the food industry. These insights provide valuable guidance for decision-makers seeking to optimize production efficiency and reduce downtime through predictive maintenance strategies.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Learning Styles on OpenEdx Using Trace Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: In a learning management system (LMS), the tutor does not interact with the students in person to interpret their reactions and grimaces or to determine the level of course assimilation. As a result, analyzing learners' behavior and traces in an e-learning environment has become necessary for tutors or teachers to assist their students. Many researchers argue that learners' learning styles are an important factor to consider in LMS. These learning styles enable students to tailor their learning to their specific environment. Every learner has a unique learning style and way of perceiving, processing, retaining, and comprehending new information. This approach, which is based on the analysis of learners' interaction traces in LMS, gives teachers a sense of their students' behavior and identifies their learning styles. Our method has demonstrated an accuracy rate of 80% in detecting learning styles, significantly enhancing engagement and motivation. By tailoring content, activities, and assessments to match each student's preferences, we can adapt interventions dynamically.

articleTitle: Designing, Optimizing, and Manufacturing of Horizontal Wind Turbine Blades Using the Available Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: The research aims to enhance wind turbine blade performance by utilizing available technologies and considering constraints such as limited resources. The focus is on developing blade designs that optimize material use, manufacturing techniques, and performance while reducing costs. Alternative and cost-effective materials are considered for blade manufacturing. Analytical models and computational simulations are deployed to validate the initial design and analyze multiple parameters. Simulations and mold production are conducted before manufacturing the blades. Assembly, installation, and testing processes evaluate blade performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing MANETs Security Against Black Hole Attacks through Time-Based Node Analysis in AOMDV Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Mobile ad-hoc networks (MANETs) rely solely on direct node communication and function without a fixed infrastructure. Due to their decentralized design, they are susceptible to numerous security risks, with black hole attacks posing significant threats to routing integrity and confidentiality. This paper proposes a technique to enhance the Ad hoc On-Demand Multi-path Distance Vector (AOMDV) routing protocol's security against black hole attacks. The method involves a time-based reply message analysis to identify and mitigate malicious nodes. This algorithm improves the protocol's ability to detect and prevent black hole attacks by closely analyzing response time differences between malicious and normal nodes. The results of the simulation show that the suggested solution greatly enhances network performance by lowering the Routing Overhead Ratio from 1388.04% to 0.73% and the Packet Loss Rate from 74% to 11% while keeping a high Packet Delivery Ratio—up to 93% in different scenarios. These enhancements sustain strong data transmission in dynamic MANET environments, supporting network integrity and reliability.

articleTitle: Sensorless Direct Torque Control in Brushless DC Motor Using Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Smart Technologies and Applications (eSmarTA)
abstract: Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motors have obvious advantages such as simple structure, low cost, high output torque, and high efficiency, making them more widely used than other types of motors. Control strategies for BLDC motors necessitate rotor position; however, position sensors are susceptible to malfunctions that can incapacitate the entire motor system. Furthermore, commutation torque pulsation in BLDC motors constrains their application, contributing to vibration and noise during prolonged operation. To address these issues, a sensorless direct torque control (DTC) strategy is devised by integrating position estimation by a proposed sliding mode observer (SMO) with direct torque control (DTC) technology. This strategy estimates the back electromotive force and speed to calculate the instantaneous electromagnetic torque applied to the BLDC motor and restricts the torque ripple to approximately 0.25 N.m. Simulation verification confirms the feasibility of the strategy.
